name: Meta DeKalb Data Center
summary: Meta campus at 2050 Metaverse Way on the south side of DeKalb, Illinois, off Interstate 88. Meta broke ground in 2020 on a planned five-building campus of more than 2.3 million sq ft and more than USD 1 billion of investment. It came online in late November 2023, when the Illinois governor attended the opening; local reports said two buildings were serving traffic and about 1 million sq ft had been built. Meta says it planned its energy needs with ComEd and pays the full cost of the energy the campus uses.

location.note: Mean of three building outlines tagged as Meta-operated data centers in the local OpenStreetMap layer (ways 1312792611, 1312792612, 1312792613) on DeKalb's south side, consistent with the cited address on Metaverse Way off I-88. The point is a building centroid average, not a surveyed parcel.

notes: At the November 2023 opening, the state release called the campus fully operational, while local reports said two of five planned buildings were serving traffic and about 1 million of 2.3 million sq ft had been built; the status follows the building-level reporting. No later report on the remaining buildings was found. Meta's fact sheet (s1) shows no publication date; its embedded file creation date is 2026-09-02.

parties.name: City of DeKalb
parties.note: Partnered with Meta and ComEd on serving the campus; Meta says it pays the full cost of city water and wastewater service.

metrics.note: Space reported as built at the November 2023 opening, when two of the five planned buildings were serving traffic.
Skilled trade workers during construction; Meta's fact sheet gives 1,200 at peak.
Once fully operational; about 80 people were employed at the opening.

milestones.note: Opening ceremony; the first two buildings began carrying live traffic that week.

power_sources.description: Served by ComEd, which partnered with Meta and the City of DeKalb to power the campus; Meta says it planned its energy needs with the utility and pays the full cost of the energy used, and the state release says the data center is supported by 100% renewable energy.
